data.title: Squamous cell carcinoma — viva
data.summary: Premalignant & malignant tumours · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Squamous cell carcinoma** (Premalignant & malignant tumours)_

**Q1. Define cutaneous SCC (cSCC).**
- Malignant tumour of epidermal keratinocytes with invasion into the dermis, capable of local destruction and metastasis (2–5% overall; higher in high-risk tumours); second commonest skin cancer worldwide; in India often arises on chronic scars/ulcers and in genital or oral mucosa

**Q2. Describe SCC: types and risk factors (PYQ).**
- Risk factors: cumulative UV exposure, fair skin, age, chronic immunosuppression (organ transplant — 65–250× risk; azathioprine, voriconazole), HPV (periungual/genital — 16, 18; β-HPV in EDV), ionising radiation, arsenic, tar, mineral oils, PUVA, smoking (lip), chronic inflammation and scars (burns — Marjolin's ulcer, lupus vulgaris, DLE, chronic ulcers, osteomyelitis sinus, lichen sclerosus, erosive LP, DEB, HS), Kangri cancer (Kashmir — abdominal wall from fire pot), Kang cancer, dhoti cancer (waist), chutta cancer (reverse smoking — palate), betel/tobacco chewing (oral), xeroderma pigmentosum, albinism, BRAF inhibitors (keratoacanthoma-like)
- Precursors: actinic keratosis, Bowen's disease (SCC in situ), actinic cheilitis, leukoplakia/erythroplakia, erythroplasia of Queyrat (glans), bowenoid papulosis, arsenical keratoses, porokeratosis

**Q3. Clinical types.**
- In situ: Bowen's disease — slowly enlarging, well-defined, red scaly plaque (lower legs of elderly women, trunk); erythroplasia of Queyrat (velvety red plaque on glans of uncircumcised men)
- Invasive: indurated keratotic nodule or plaque, ulcer with raised everted indurated edges, cutaneous horn, verrucous/exophytic, bleeding; sun-exposed sites (ear, lip, scalp, dorsum of hand) or on scars
- Variants: keratoacanthoma (well-differentiated SCC variant — rapidly growing crateriform nodule with central keratin plug in weeks, may regress), verrucous carcinoma (low-grade — oral florid papillomatosis, Buschke–Löwenstein (genital), epithelioma cuniculatum (plantar)), spindle-cell, acantholytic, adenosquamous, desmoplastic (aggressive)

**Q4. Histopathology.**
- Irregular nests and strands of atypical squamous cells invading the dermis from the epidermis, keratin pearls, intercellular bridges, dyskeratosis, mitoses
- Broders' grading by differentiation: well (>75% differentiated), moderately, poorly (<25%), undifferentiated
- Keratoacanthoma: symmetric cup-shaped crater filled with keratin, glassy eosinophilic cells, buttresses ('lipping') at edges

**Q5. High-risk features.**
- Diameter ≥2 cm, depth >6 mm or beyond subcutaneous fat, poor differentiation, perineural invasion (nerve ≥0.1 mm), desmoplastic/acantholytic subtype, location — ear, lip, temple, H-zone, genital; arising in scar/chronic ulcer or radiation site; immunosuppression; recurrent tumour; rapid growth
- Staging: AJCC 8th (head and neck) and Brigham and Women's Hospital (T1–T3 by risk factors)

**Q6. Differential diagnosis.**
- Keratoacanthoma, BCC, AK (hypertrophic), wart, seborrhoeic keratosis (irritated), amelanotic melanoma, Merkel cell carcinoma, pyogenic granuloma, prurigo nodule, chronic infections (TBVC, chromoblastomycosis, deep fungal, mycetoma, leishmaniasis — pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia mimics SCC)

**Q7. Investigations.**
- Biopsy (incisional/excisional) including deep tissue; examine regional lymph nodes; FNAC/USG of nodes; CT/MRI for deep invasion, perineural spread or nodal disease; sentinel lymph node biopsy (selected high-risk)

**Q8. Management.**
- Low-risk: surgical excision with 4–6 mm margins; curettage and electrodesiccation for small low-risk; cryotherapy for in situ
- High-risk: wide excision with ≥6 mm margins or Mohs surgery; adjuvant radiotherapy for perineural invasion/positive margins/nodal disease; nodal dissection for nodal metastasis
- Bowen's disease: 5-FU, imiquimod, PDT, cryotherapy, curettage, excision
- Advanced/metastatic or unresectable: immune checkpoint inhibitors — cemiplimab (first approved), pembrolizumab; EGFR inhibitor cetuximab; platinum chemotherapy (older)
- Prevention: sun protection, treat precursors, nicotinamide, acitretin in transplant recipients, switch immunosuppressant to sirolimus (mTOR inhibitor)
- Follow-up: 3–6 monthly for 2 years then yearly; skin and node examination

**Q9. Discuss cutaneous markers of internal malignancy (PYQ).**
- Paraneoplastic dermatoses: acanthosis nigricans (malignant), tripe palms, Leser–Trélat sign, acrokeratosis paraneoplastica of Bazex (SCC upper aerodigestive tract), erythema gyratum repens (lung), necrolytic migratory erythema (glucagonoma), hypertrichosis lanuginosa acquisita, dermatomyositis, paraneoplastic pemphigus, Sweet syndrome/pyoderma gangrenosum (haematological), Trousseau's migratory thrombophlebitis (pancreas), carcinoid flushing, multicentric reticulohistiocytosis, pachydermoperiostosis, ichthyosis acquisita (lymphoma), extramammary Paget's
- Genetic syndromes with skin markers: Gardner, Muir–Torre (sebaceous tumours), Cowden (trichilemmomas), Peutz–Jeghers, Birt–Hogg–Dubé, Gorlin, MEN 2B (mucosal neuromas), Howel–Evans, Carney complex

## Quick spotter facts
- Ulcer with raised everted indurated edge on old burn scar — Marjolin's SCC
- Keratin pearls, Broders' grading
- Kangri cancer — Kashmir

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Squamous cell carcinoma; keratoacanthoma); Brigham and Women's / AJCC staging concepts. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
